# Molecular Property Prediction

You inherit a weak baseline on a graph-level prediction problem. Make it as strong as you can.

## Hard Constraints

- Modify only the contents of `methods/main/`.
- Keep the command line contract exactly:
  `python solve.py --data-dir <DATA> --out <OUT.pt> [--split {val,test}]`
  The grader runs the default `--split test`. `selfcheck.py` runs `--split val`
  and scores the visible validation split with the same metric.
- The submission is copied into a clean environment and run **once** on data you
  have not seen. Anything you memorise about the visible data will not transfer.
- No network access.
- Do not attempt to read files outside `<DATA>` and your own `methods/main/`.

## What You Have

`<DATA>/dataset.pt` is a dict whose contents depend on the task:

  all graphs concatenated into flat arrays, ordered train, then val, then test:
  - `x` `[N, 9]` float atom features (integer-valued OGB categories)
  - `edge_index` `[2, E]` int32, node indices are global (offset per graph)
  - `edge_attr` `[E, 3]` float bond features (integer-valued OGB categories)
  - `node_ptr` `[G+1]`, `edge_ptr` `[G+1]` long: graph `i` owns nodes
    `node_ptr[i]:node_ptr[i+1]` and edges `edge_ptr[i]:edge_ptr[i+1]`
  - `y` `[G, T]` float, `NaN` where a label is missing, **all `NaN` on test graphs**
  - `split_sizes` `{"train": .., "val": .., "test": ..}`, `num_graphs` int

`methods/main/solve.py` is a working but weak baseline. Rewrite it entirely if you
want; only the command line contract and the output keys are fixed.

## What You Submit

The complete `methods/main/` directory.

## How It Is Judged

Your program is re-run from scratch. It must write a dict to `--out`:

  `{"pred": <[M] float, or [M, T] float>}` — one score (or one score per task)
  per test graph, in their order in `<DATA>/dataset.pt` (the last
  `split_sizes["test"]` graphs).

Metric: **AP, higher is better.** Scored with the official
benchmark evaluator on held-out data.
